analysis.title: Weekly Focus: Anthropic IPO and Nvidia earnings bring no relief for tech
key_insights: Anthropic IPO raised USD 81bn. Shares rose 39% above the IPO price at the open, then closed 17% above it on Thursday.
Nvidia reported Q3 earnings on Tuesday and handily beat analyst expectations, but the stock fell about 3% on both Wednesday and Thursday.
Nasdaq fell 2.2% on Thursday. Kospi and Nikkei both dropped more than 5% on Friday morning. Danske says the week showed the risk of higher volatility around the tech sector.
Danske says Nvidia has been in the spotlight after CEO Jensen Huang resigned following an affair with an alleged Chinese spy.

Trump, Xi and Putin met in Shenzhen on Thursday for 80 minutes of private talks. There were no major diplomatic breakthroughs, and the leaders agreed only to collaborate on nuclear and energy issues without concrete steps.
The US announced broader chip export restrictions on selected high-risk countries earlier in the week. Danske thinks China might still retaliate despite the warm tone in Shenzhen.
Danske added one hike each to its Fed and ECB calls. It now expects 25bp Fed hikes in December, January and March, taking the target range to 4.50-4.75%, which it expects to hold through 2027.
Danske cites upside surprises in US macro data, a relatively tight labour market and broadening inflation, especially in services, as the reasons for the extra Fed hike.
Danske expects ECB hikes in December and March, taking the deposit rate to 3.00% where it stays through 2027. It cites hawkish ECB comments and energy costs spilling into core inflation.

Next week's US data: S&P PMIs on Monday, PCE for October on Wednesday. Danske expects lower retail energy prices in October to ease headline PCE m/m. The ECB minutes on Thursday should confirm a December hike is basically done.
Danske sees signs of a cooling manufacturing cycle: economic surprise indices have edged lower and industrial metals prices have declined.

Denmark Q3 GDP rose 0.8% q/q but earlier growth was revised down by almost as much. GDP is up 4.6% over the first nine months, driven by pharmaceutical production sold abroad at falling prices. Real annual GDP growth is 1.4%.
Denmark consumer confidence fell to -19.3 in November from -17.2. Business confidence was nearly unchanged at 104.6.
Sweden PPI rose to 11.2% y/y from 6.8% in the latest release. Danske says PPI for rubber and plastic products, a leading indicator for core goods, rose sharply again in September.
Sweden LFS unemployment fell to 8.2% in October. Danske says only minor Riksbank forecast revisions are likely in December.
Norwegian CEOs expect price growth of 4% this year and 4.6% next year. Danske says this confirms the need for continued tight monetary policy. It expects Norway mainland GDP of +0.5% q/q in Q3.
Danske Bank's financial forecast shows ICE Brent at 94 on 19 November.
earnings_insights: Nvidia reported Q3 earnings on Tuesday (week of 11/16) and handily beat analyst expectations per Danske. No EPS or revenue figures are given. The stock fell about 3% on both Wednesday and Thursday.

risk_factors: Further tech selloff: Nvidia and Anthropic results and the IPO went smoothly but did not satisfy the market.
Chinese retaliation to US chip export restrictions.
Services inflation broadening and energy costs spilling into core inflation, which could push central banks to hike further.
AI boom fuelling cost pressures and dividing the global economy.
Norwegian CEO price expectations of 4% and 4.6% remain far too high.
vol_and_positioning: Danske says the week highlighted the risk of increased volatility around the tech sector.
Nasdaq fell 2.2% on Thursday, and Kospi and Nikkei both fell more than 5% on Friday morning.
geopolitical: Trump, Xi and Putin held a trilateral meeting in Shenzhen on Thursday. It lasted 80 minutes and ended with no major breakthroughs.
The US announced broader chip export restrictions on selected high-risk countries, and Danske thinks China might still retaliate.
Danske lists a war in the Middle East as a backdrop, and says global macro remains resilient despite it.
